title: Prelink and isolate shared objects to reduce GPU runtime jitter
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem:
Runtime cold-start and inter-node latency variance during model inference has been traced to dynamic linker symbol resolution and on-demand initialization of GPU shared objects (libcudnn, libcublasLt, libcutlass, triton plugins). This causes measurable jitter in our P95/P99 tail latency for short-sequence workloads and complicates autoscaling decisions.

Goal:
Create a deterministic, reproducible startup path for critical GPU shared objects that reduces first-request latency variance and startup jitter across heterogeneous nodes without regressing memory usage or breaking compatibility with existing private deployments.

Proposed approach summary:
1) Introduce a controlled "prelink/preload" boot step in the runtime agent that dlopens a curated list of GPU libraries with RTLD_NOW and forces critical symbol binds. This will be gated behind a feature flag and enabled only for candidate pools during canary.
2) Build a small symbol-isolation shim (shim-loader) per model family that exposes a stable internal symbol facade (SONAME-preserving) so different CUTLASS/TRITON variants can coexist. The shim will also support a NO_INIT mode to skip heavyweight static constructors during canary warmup where needed.
3) Produce a deterministic loader ordering manifest as part of the kernel bundle (manifest.json) and include it in our signed kernel bundles to reduce nondeterministic linker resolution order.
4) Add CI jobs to produce lightweight prelinked artifacts (linker map) and run compatibility smoke tests across existing CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS ABI groups.

Key technical considerations and trade-offs:
- Using RTLD_NOW increases startup CPU cost; acceptable for cold-start but must be optional for steady-state container reuse. We'll make use of a per-instance policy: prelink on cold-start only or on dedicated-pool warmup nodes.
- Prelinking techniques like system prelink are deprecated; we will implement application-level deterministic dlopen ordering and a small symbol-stub generator during build to avoid system-level tooling.
- Shim complexity: maintain backwards compatibility by keeping SONAMEs stable and providing transparent fallbacks when symbol mismatches detected. This may add ~1-2% memory overhead per process.
- Security: loader changes require a security review because they touch native linking. See security_review_required below.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- M1 (Design + Spec): Consolidate library list, manifest schema, and shim API (owner: Jonah) — due 2026-03-17.
- M2 (Prototype): Implement prelink step in runtime-agent + simple shim for libcutlass and triton_plugin; add smoke test harness — due 2026-03-24.
- M3 (Canary): Enable on small dedicated pool, collect P50/P95/P99 and memory metrics for 72h, iterate on ordering — due 2026-04-01.
- M4 (Rollout + CI): Add prelinked artifact generation to release pipeline, add compatibility matrix tests, documentation — due 2026-04-15.

Acceptance criteria:
- P95 tail latency for short-seq (<=64 tokens) workloads reduced by >=10% on canary pools compared to baseline within 72h of canary run.
- Cold-start latency variance (standard deviation of first-request latency) reduced by >=20% across the canary fleet.
- No regression in functional tests for at least 3 canonical models (GPT-like LLM, T5 family, small quantized embedder).
- Compatibility tests across 3 CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS matrix cells pass in CI (CUDA 12.2+Triton2.1, CUDA 11.8+Triton1.10, CUDA 13+Triton3 preview).

Rollout plan:
- Stage A: Internal dev pool (2 nodes) with feature-flagged prelink enabled, run nightly synthetic workload for 48-72h.
- Stage B: Canary dedicated pool (5% of dedicated capacity), compare telemetry against control, collect CI & RUM traces.
- Stage C: Gradual increase to 25% then 100% for dedicated pools; hosted API will be opt-in per model tag for initial release.
- Rollback: Feature flag off and restart agent to drop preloaded handles; a hot-fallback that switches to lazy dlopen for a requested model is implemented.

Testing and telemetry:
- Add a telemetry tag prelink_v1 and emit prelink.status, prelink.duration_ms, prelink.forced_bind_count.
- Add a dashboard widget: Runtime -> Startup -> Prelink Canary (link in links).
- Add CI matrix job: runtime/prelink-compat (runs across container images and kernel-bundle manifest permutations).

Documentation & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Shared+Object+Warmup+and+Shim+Design
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2345
- Canary dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/prelink-canary

Notes on compatibility guards:
- If symbol mismatch occurs during early bind, shim registers conflicting symbols and the loader falls back to an isolated namespace created via dlmopen where supported. Fallback paths will be flagged and surfaced to ops so we can add to compatibility matrix.
- Kernel bundles must include a short "loader-hints" section describing preferred loader order; bundles without hints will use conservative default ordering.

Longer-term opportunities:
- Evaluate storing a small binary snapshot of resolved symbols (linkmap) per kernel bundle to fully eliminate resolution nondeterminism.
- Investigate pre-initializing CUDA contexts and cuBLAS handles in a pool process to serve as warmup proxies for ultra-low latency use-cases.
